Kelas Kreatif AI Canva Untuk Siswa Program PkM di SMAN 1 Lebak Wangi
abstractText: Perkembangan teknologi digital dan kecerdasan buatan (Artificial Intelligence/AI) telah membuka peluang baru dalam dunia pendidikan, khususnya dalam pengembangan kreativitas dan literasi digital peserta didik. Namun, masih banyak siswa yang belum mampu memanfaatkan teknologi desain digital secara optimal untuk mendukung kegiatan pembelajaran dan pengabdian kepada masyarakat. Oleh karena itu, kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan meningkatkan pemahaman, keterampilan, dan kesiapan siswa dalam menggunakan aplikasi Canva berbasis AI melalui program Pelatihan Kelas Kreatif AI Canva bagi siswa PKM SMAN 1 Lebak Wangi. Metode pelaksanaan kegiatan meliputi ceramah, demonstrasi, praktik langsung (learning by doing), diskusi, pendampingan, dan evaluasi. Keberhasilan program diukur melalui beberapa indikator, yaitu pemahaman materi, kemudahan penggunaan Canva, proses pembuatan desain, kualitas konten, pembelajaran, kolaborasi, fasilitasi, etika dan literasi digital, serta niat menggunakan Canva. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan memberikan dampak positif yang signifikan dengan rata-rata capaian sebesar 81,4%, melampaui target yang ditetapkan sebesar 75%. Peningkatan tertinggi terjadi pada indikator kemudahan penggunaan Canva dan niat menggunakan Canva yang masing-masing mencapai 100%, menunjukkan tingginya penerimaan dan motivasi siswa dalam memanfaatkan teknologi AI. Selain itu, peserta berhasil menghasilkan berbagai karya digital berupa poster, infografis, dan media presentasi yang kreatif serta komunikatif. Kegiatan ini membuktikan bahwa pelatihan Canva berbasis AI efektif dalam meningkatkan literasi digital, kreativitas, dan keterampilan desain visual siswa. Program ini juga berkontribusi dalam mempersiapkan generasi muda yang adaptif, inovatif, dan siap menghadapi tantangan transformasi digital di era Society 5.0.

AI and computational methods for reconstructing cell-state-specific gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptome and chromatin accessibility data in cancer: methods, applications, and perspectives
abstractText: Tumor heterogeneity is shaped by genetic, epigenetic, microenvironmental, and stochastic factors, among which cell-state-specific regulatory programs are a major determinant. Gene regulatory networks provide a systems-level model linking transcription factors, cis-regulatory elements, and target genes. Paired single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq) measure chromatin accessibility and gene expression in the same cell, offering a direct view of regulatory elements and transcriptional output; matched-but-unpaired, imputed, and single-modality designs can extend coverage but introduce additional assumptions and artifacts. This mini-review focuses on AI and computational methods for reconstructing cell-state-specific GRNs from single-cell transcriptome and chromatin accessibility data in cancer. We define inclusion criteria, distinguish same-cell paired, matched-unpaired, imputed, and single-modality designs, and organize methods by inference objective and input requirement. We cover motif/co-accessibility inference, deep integration and graph learning, dynamic and cell-state-specific modeling, and virtual perturbation. We then discuss applications in epithelial-mesenchymal transition, treatment resistance, lineage plasticity, and tumor subtyping, emphasizing an evidence hierarchy from statistical association to directional prediction, in silico perturbation, and experimentally supported causal regulation. Finally, we examine benchmarking, limitations, and translational prospects. These approaches may help convert GRNs from descriptive maps into testable models of tumor regulation, but clinical utility still requires prospective validation.

abstractText: Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan meningkatkan kapasitas kelompok pembudidaya ikan lele di Desa Kebakalan, Kecamatan Porong, Kabupaten Sidoarjo melalui digitalisasi manajemen budidaya, edukasi kesehatan ikan, serta pengembangan produk bernilai tambah. title: Lower Critical Solution Temperature-type Phase Separation Behavior of Aqueous Solutions of Structurally Uniform Stereoregular Dense Triazole Oligomers Bearing N -ethyl- N -methylamide Side Chains
abstractText: Abstract The lower critical solution temperature (LCST)-type phase separation behavior of aqueous solutions of structurally uniform stereoregular dense triazole oligomers bearing N-ethyl-N-methylamide side chains was investigated using two series of oligomer samples: TBDMS-syndio-ME nOH (n = 4, 6, and 8), bearing a terminal t-butyldimethylsilyl group, and syndio-ME nOH (n = 2, 4, 6, and 8), which were synthesized by stepwise copper(I)-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC). Transmittance measurements in the heating and cooling processes with stirring at 500 rpm demonstrated that TBDMS-syndio-ME nOH (n = 4, 6, and 8) exhibited LCST-type phase separation with an unusual apparent “inverse” hysteresis, in which the transmittance recovered in the cooling process at temperatures higher than the clouding point temperature (Tcloud) observed in the heating process. On the other hand, syndio-ME nOH samples remained completely soluble over the temperature range examined. Steady-state fluorescence measurements using Nile Red as a fluorescence probe indicated that TBDMS-syndio-ME nOH (n = 4, 6, and 8) samples formed micelles with lower apparent critical micelle concentrations (0.0047, 0.015, and 0.040 g L–1, respectively) in water. Dynamic light scattering measurements revealed that the micelles with apparent hydrodynamic radii of ca. 1–4 nm rapidly aggregated into micrometer-sized species around Tcloud in the heating process and were regenerated at temperatures < Tcloud in the cooling process, showing no intrinsic inverse hysteresis. Preliminary molecular dynamics simulations further indicated gradual dehydration and compaction of the micelles with increasing temperature. Based on the experimental and simulation data, we propose that the apparent “inverse” hysteresis originates from the formation of highly hydrated amorphous microdroplets produced through aggregation, rearrangement, and fusion of micelles during phase separation. The subsequent decrease in interfacial area and refractive index contrast leads to recovery of transmittance without complete dissolution of the microdroplets of the condensed phase.

Management and Marketing Frameworks in Geoheritage Research: A Structural Bibliometric Analysis
abstractText: Abstract Research on geoheritage has experienced rapid expansion in recent years. However, the integration of management and marketing perspectives remains conceptually inconsistent. This study employs bibliometric and science-mapping methodologies to characterise the indexed knowledge base on geoheritage management and marketing in the Web of Science and Scopus (1981–2025). Following record-level deduplication, the final dataset comprises N = 1344 documents. The analysis examines publication growth, citation visibility, country productivity and collaboration patterns, source and author concentration, as well as the thematic structure of the field through trend topics, co-occurrence networks, and thematic evolution over time. The findings indicate delayed yet robust consolidation since 2014 and reveal a stable conceptual framework centred on geoheritage, geoconservation, and geotourism. Furthermore, geoparks and UNESCO-related governance serve as the predominant contexts for implementation. Management is primarily operationalised through inventorying, assessment, and decision-making frameworks geared towards conservation. In contrast, explicit marketing constructs exhibit limited structural centrality within keyword and abstract-level networks. Themes related to marketing are primarily manifest through discourses on tourism, interpretation, communication, and digital engagement, rather than through clearly articulated marketing theories or behavioural mechanisms. These results, therefore, suggest a comparatively weak lexical integration of formal marketing theory within the indexed geoheritage corpus. The study identifies opportunities for more precise integration within behavioural and marketing theory, emphasises a more systematic evaluation of management and communication interventions, and advocates for broader empirical coverage beyond geopark-centric research contexts.

A Dual pH‑Responsive Hydrogel with Site‑Specific Therapeutic Functions for Differential Pathological Microenvironment Remodeling and Accelerated Repair of Infected Diabetic Wounds
abstractText: Abstract Diabetic skin wounds have disrupted local acid–base balance, prone to bacterial adhesion and sustained chronic inflammation that hinders tissue repair. Benefiting from the unique properties of oxidized sodium alginate, we prepared a dual pH-responsive Schiff base crosslinked hydrogel loaded with herbal nanoparticles to remodel the defective wound microenvironment and speed up regeneration. Dynamic covalent crosslinking endows the hydrogel with favorable flexibility and shape adaptability to fit irregular wound surfaces. It exhibits obvious dual pH sensitivity: strong antibacterial activity in bacteria-rich acidic niches and slow hydrolysis under diabetic wound alkalinity, achieving stable drug release without burst leakage. The encapsulated nanoparticles exhibit multiple complementary functions. Zn2+ acts as an efficient bactericide to eliminate pathogens. L-Arginine facilitates nitric oxide (NO) generation to promote angiogenesis and M2 macrophage polarization. The glycyrrhetinic acid-2-hydroxyacetophenone conjugate (GA-HAP) suppresses proinflammatory cytokines to relieve local inflammation. In vitro and in vivo experiments verify that this composite hydrogel balances wound pH, eradicates bacterial infection, and mitigates persistent inflammation, remarkably accelerating diabetic wound healing. This pH-sensitive herbal hydrogel holds great potential for microenvironment regulation and clinical therapy of intractable diabetic wounds.
